teaching_objective: Identify a CISM stem's qualifier before evaluating any answer choice, and correctly state what kind of reasoning test that qualifier requires (prerequisite, immediate-next-action, completeness-of-fit, priority-ranking, or fundamental-purpose).
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer is determined by first identifying which qualifier word the stem uses (or that none is present) and what specific reasoning test that qualifier requires — not by evaluating which answer choice sounds most generally correct or most technically sound.
note: PHASE 6C CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 6C architecture. qualifier_target is deliberately null: this family tests the qualifier-recognition SKILL generically, so its three variants each exercise a DIFFERENT canonical qualifier (NEXT, FIRST, BEST) rather than repeating one — this is the family's own primary variation axis, not a gap. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that in a CISM governance/accountability scenario, decision authority belongs to whoever is accountable for that specific outcome — not to whoever identified, analyzed, or recommended it, regardless of their expertise.
invariant_reasoning: Across every scenario in this family, a role that merely identified, analyzed, or recommended the issue — most often the security manager — is offered as the tempting wrong answer. The correct answer is always the role actually accountable for that specific decision's outcome. Which role that is varies scenario to scenario (business/process owner, risk owner, Board/senior management) and must be reasoned from the stem's own accountability chain, not assumed from a fixed hierarchy — this is a deliberate content-design choice, not an omission: see docs/learning/ROLE-AUTHORITY-MATRIX.md's explicit instruction not to encode a fixed role-always-decides rule.
note: PHASE 6C CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 6C architecture, grounded in docs/learning/PATTERN-LIBRARY.md (P02, P03), docs/learning/ROLE-AUTHORITY-MATRIX.md, and docs/learning/DOMAIN-1-BLUEPRINT.md. role_target names the recurring DISTRACTOR (security manager), not a fixed correct answer — the correct role is scenario-dependent by design, per the invariant_reasoning field. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Correctly classify a described activity as GOVERNANCE (direction, accountability, oversight, resource stewardship) or MANAGEMENT (execution within that direction), regardless of how technically detailed or significant the management activity sounds.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer is whichever option sets direction, accepts accountability, or exercises ongoing oversight at the enterprise level — not whichever option merely executes, configures, assesses, or selects within a scope governance has already approved, no matter how effortful or important that execution sounds.
note: PHASE 7B-1 CANDIDATE (D1-U1) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-1 scope. role_target is null because this family's variation axis is the ACTIVITY being classified (risk appetite, budget/objectives, oversight reporting), not a recurring distractor role. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Governance Layer Authority (Board, Steering Committee, CISO)
teaching_objective: Match the requested verb (fund, prioritize, accept, approve, advocate, develop, recommend) to the governance-layer body — Board/Senior Management, Security Steering Committee, or CISO/Security Manager — that actually performs it, given each variant's organizational context.
invariant_reasoning: Across every scenario in this family, at least two of the three governance-layer bodies are genuinely involved in the decision, and the tempting wrong answer is whichever body is involved but does not hold the specific authority the stem's verb requires. Which body is correct varies scenario to scenario (Board/senior management for funding and risk acceptance; the steering committee for cross-functional prioritization; the CISO for development, assessment, and recommendation) and must be reasoned from the verb in the stem, not assumed from a fixed hierarchy — this deliberately extends family.d1.authority-accountability-decision's same non-fixed-hierarchy design choice to a three-body governance layer instead of a single recurring distractor.
note: PHASE 7B-1 CANDIDATE (D1-U3) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-1 scope. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong body genuinely varies per variant (sometimes the steering committee, sometimes the CISO) rather than being one fixed recurring distractor — this IS the family's variation axis (role-mix), not a gap. 4 initial variants per the approved Phase 7A/7B-1 decision (above the 3-variant floor, given this is the source bank's single largest reasoning cluster). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Data Ownership & Information Asset Accountability
teaching_objective: Recognize that the accountable business-side data/information owner — not IT, security, a vendor, or a custodian — classifies information, defines its protection requirements, and approves access, across classification, access-approval, and protection-requirement decisions.
invariant_reasoning: Across every scenario in this family, a technically-proximate role — IT, the security manager, a system vendor, a custodian, or an outsourced cloud provider — is offered as the tempting wrong answer because they are visibly close to the data. The correct answer is always the accountable business-side data/information owner, reasoned from who bears the business impact of that information, not from who technically stores, secures, or administers it.
note: PHASE 7B-1 CANDIDATE (D1-U4) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-1 scope. role_target is null because the tempting technical-role distractor deliberately varies per variant (IT, security manager, vendor, custodian, cloud provider) per the explicit Phase 7B-1 instruction to vary the distractor. 4 initial variants per the approved Phase 7A/7B-1 decision. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that an information security strategy must be driven by and aligned with business objectives, priorities, and risk appetite, and distinguish strategic direction from implementation detail.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always traces the security strategy back to the enterprise's stated business objective, priority, or risk-appetite context - never to which option is technically strongest, broadest, or most comprehensive in isolation from that context.
note: PHASE 7B-2 CANDIDATE (D1-U5) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-2 scope. role_target is null because this family's variation axis is the business scenario (expansion, organizational change, investment prioritization), not a recurring distractor role. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Business Justification, Business Cases & Roadmaps
teaching_objective: Distinguish strategy, business case, and roadmap by purpose, and recognize that security initiatives are justified by connecting them to business value, risk, cost, and priorities - not by security benefit alone or by ROI alone.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always identifies the specific business-justification or planning artifact/reasoning the scenario actually calls for - a business case connecting investment to value/risk/cost, a roadmap sequencing approved direction over time, or qualitative risk reasoning where ROI can't be precisely quantified - never a generic 'it's good for security' or 'ROI is the only valid basis' answer.
note: PHASE 7B-2 CANDIDATE (D1-U6) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-2 scope. role_target is null because this family's variation axis is which business-justification/planning reasoning the scenario calls for (business case vs. roadmap vs. qualitative risk justification), not a recurring distractor role. Activates the Business Case vs. Strategy vs. Roadmap confusing-concept pair approved in Phase 7A. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Governance Effectiveness (Frameworks, Standards, GRC, Measurement)
teaching_objective: Recognize that frameworks, standards, and GRC mechanisms create structure and consistency but do not by themselves prove governance effectiveness - effectiveness requires outcome-focused measurement, not activity counts or structural adoption alone.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always distinguishes the structural/activity layer (adopting a framework, running GRC, completing assessments) from the outcome layer (whether the intended risk/business result was actually achieved) - the tempting wrong answer treats structure or activity volume as if it were proof of effectiveness.
note: PHASE 7B-2 CANDIDATE (D1-U7) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-2 scope, kept as one combined family per the explicit instruction not to split U7 preemptively. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong pattern is structure/activity-as-proof-of-effectiveness, not a recurring distractor role. Deliberately not a framework-cataloging family: named frameworks (ISO 27001) appear only where source-supported and only to illustrate the reasoning, not to be memorized. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Legal, Regulatory & Contractual Requirements as Risk
teaching_objective: Reason about a new legal, regulatory, or contractual requirement as a risk-management question - determining applicability, scope, and affected business processes before any treatment decision - rather than treating the mere existence of a compliance obligation as an automatic trigger for immediate implementation or as itself the answer.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always reflects structured management reasoning about the obligation - assessing applicability/scope/exposure, matching the verb to the correct role (Legal/Compliance interprets; the security manager assesses impact, advises, and coordinates; the accountable business/senior-management authority decides), and never treating 'it's a compliance requirement' as a magic answer-selection word. The tempting wrong answer varies scenario to scenario: jumping to implementation before scope assessment, assigning interpretation/decision authority to the wrong role, treating compliance as binary/absolute regardless of actual scope, or assuming one obligation (internal policy or external law) automatically overrides the other without analysis.
note: PHASE 7B-3 CANDIDATE (D1-U8) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-3 scope. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong role varies per variant (Legal/Compliance, the security manager, or the accountable business/senior-management authority can each be misassigned a verb that isn't theirs), matching the same non-fixed-hierarchy design already established by family.d1.authority-accountability-decision and family.d1.governance-layer-authority. decision_type is decision.risk because the family's whole premise is that compliance obligations are reasoned about as risk, not as a separate category. PHASE 7C UPDATE (Domain 1 readiness follow-up, G3): version bumped 1 -> 2; pattern.p08 (Risk-Driven Prioritization) added to reflect the new fourth variant's risk-based-prioritization reasoning target, matching the precedent already set by family.d1.business-justification-roadmap's use of p08 in Domain 1. All three original variants unchanged. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Organizational Culture and Governance Effectiveness
teaching_objective: Recognize that organizational culture - adoption, behavior, resistance to change, and leadership tone/consistency - determines whether governance is actually effective in practice, and that neither 'management already mandated it' nor 'send more training' is automatically the complete answer; the scenario's own stated problem (missing direction/accountability vs. missing adoption/engagement) determines what response is actually appropriate.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always traces back to what the scenario explicitly describes as missing or broken - inconsistent leadership behavior, unaddressed resistance, or a cultural/contextual adoption gap - and responds to that specific gap, never to a fixed reflex answer. The tempting wrong answer is always a reflex: assuming a published mandate is automatically sufficient, reaching for a purely technical/disciplinary fix to what is actually a leadership or cultural problem, or repeating an already-delivered generic action (like identical training) without addressing the stated reason it did not work.
note: PHASE 7B-3 CANDIDATE (D1-U9, Domain 1 capstone) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 7A architecture and Phase 7B-3 scope. role_target is null because this family's variation axis is which cultural/behavioral gap the scenario describes (resistance, leadership-tone inconsistency, cross-cultural adoption variance), not a recurring distractor role. Deliberately not a general HR/change-management family - scoped to the governance-effectiveness question extended to the cultural layer. PHASE 7C UPDATE (Domain 1 readiness follow-up, G4): version bumped 1 -> 2 for the new fourth variant, which closes the gap the Phase 7C read-only assessment identified between this family's own teaching_objective (which already asserted culture shapes 'how risk appetite is expressed in decisions') and its variants (none of which had actually tested that link). All three original variants unchanged. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 1 — Policy, Standard, Procedure & Guideline Hierarchy
teaching_objective: Correctly classify a described governance artifact as a policy, standard, procedure, or guideline based on its authority, prescriptiveness, and level of detail - not by memorizing four dictionary definitions or assuming a fixed document count every enterprise must maintain identically.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always follows the artifact's actual authority and prescriptiveness as described in the stem - mandatory, high-level management direction is a policy; a mandatory boundary or requirement supporting that policy is a standard; the specific mandatory steps taken to meet a standard or policy are a procedure; recommended, non-mandatory practice is a guideline. The tempting wrong answer confuses two adjacent artifacts in the hierarchy (most often policy/standard or procedure/guideline) because both sound like they describe 'a requirement' or both sound like they describe 'how to do something,' without reasoning about actual authority and prescriptiveness.
note: PHASE 7C CANDIDATE (Domain 1 readiness follow-up, G1) — authored by Claude Code per architect decision following the Phase 7C read-only assessment's finding that docs/learning/DOMAIN-1-BLUEPRINT.md's canonical 'must accomplish' requirement (recognize the policy/standard/procedure/guideline hierarchy) was not yet taught anywhere in Domain 1. Taught inside lesson.d1.governance-effectiveness (U7) rather than a new unit, per explicit instruction; tested via this dedicated family rather than folded into family.d1.governance-effectiveness's own variants, since artifact classification is a distinct reasoning target from that family's activity-vs-outcome target. decision_type is decision.program-control because the family's premise (how security requirements become policies, standards, procedures, and operating practices) matches that decision type's own registry definition almost verbatim. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that risk is the combination of a credible threat, an exploitable vulnerability, and the business impact if the two came together - not any one of these three alone, and not a raw vulnerability count.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always connects threat, vulnerability, and business impact together to determine actual risk; the tempting wrong answer treats one input alone (vulnerability count, threat presence, or a system simply being new) as if it were equivalent to risk.
note: PHASE 9B-1 CANDIDATE (D2-U1, Domain 2 entry point) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-1 scope. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong pattern is a vulnerability-count/single-input-as-risk trap, not a recurring distractor role. One variant illustrates emerging risk via an AI scenario, per the explicit Phase 9B-1 instruction that AI must appear only as one source-supported example, not a dedicated topic. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Risk Assessment Lifecycle (Context, Identify, Analyze, Evaluate)
teaching_objective: Locate which of the risk lifecycle's Context/Identify/Analyze/Evaluate stages a scenario describes, and recognize that each stage depends on the one before it having actually happened.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always reasons from exactly what the stem states has and hasn't happened yet to identify the correct current or next lifecycle stage; the tempting wrong answer skips ahead to a later stage's action (treatment, evaluation, ownership) before the stem's own facts support it.
note: PHASE 9B-1 CANDIDATE (D2-U2) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-1 scope. stage_target is null at the family level because the three variants deliberately span different stages/transitions (Context->Identify sequencing, Identify-stage prerequisite reasoning, Analyze-vs-Evaluate distinction), not one single fixed stage. Deliberately stops at Evaluate; Treat and later stages are out of scope for this batch. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Risk Analysis Methods (Qualitative vs. Quantitative)
teaching_objective: Select the assessment method (qualitative or quantitative) that fits the decision's actual objective, rather than assuming quantitative is inherently superior or more rigorous.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always matches the method to what the decision actually needs (a fast relative ranking, a defensible dollar comparison, or an honest description of something that doesn't quantify well) - the tempting wrong answer treats one method as universally better, more rigorous, or more consistent regardless of the decision at hand.
note: PHASE 9B-2 CANDIDATE (D2-U3) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-2 scope. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong pattern is a method-selection bias (quantitative-is-always-better, false precision, consistency-over-fit), not a recurring distractor role. stage_target is stage.risk.analyze because all three variants concern which analysis technique to use, a decision made within the Analyze stage. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Quantitative Risk for Decisions (AV, EF, SLE, ARO, ALE)
teaching_objective: Compute Single Loss Expectancy and Annualized Loss Expectancy from given Asset Value, Exposure Factor, and Annualized Rate of Occurrence values, and use the resulting ALE to inform - not automatically make - a treatment decision.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always correctly distinguishes ONE EVENT (SLE = AV x EF) from ONE YEAR (ALE = SLE x ARO) and treats a calculated ALE as one legitimate input into a treatment decision, never as the automatic decision itself; the tempting wrong answer conflates SLE with ALE, misreads a stated frequency as the wrong ARO, or treats a cost-vs-ALE comparison as sufficient by itself to approve or reject a control.
note: PHASE 9B-2 CANDIDATE (D2-U4) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture, Phase 9B-2 scope, and the CANONICAL quantitative-risk requirement in docs/learning/DOMAIN-2-BLUEPRINT.md. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong pattern is a calculation/interpretation error, not a recurring distractor role. Deliberately three variants of genuinely different sub-skill (calculate SLE; calculate ALE with a source-evidenced ARO-misreading trap; interpret a calculated ALE in a treatment decision), not three variants differing only by numbers, per explicit instruction. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Risk Evaluation (Appetite, Tolerance, Acceptability, Authority)
teaching_objective: Compare an already-analyzed risk against organizational criteria, appetite, and tolerance to determine acceptability, and recognize that the acceptability decision belongs to the accountable business/risk authority, not whoever performed the analysis.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always treats analysis and evaluation as separate steps (an analyzed risk is not automatically an evaluated or accepted one) and routes the acceptability decision to the accountable authority for that specific risk; the tempting wrong answer either jumps straight to treatment, conflates appetite with tolerance, or assumes a fixed role (security manager, board) always decides regardless of context.
note: PHASE 9B-3 CANDIDATE (D2-U5) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-3 scope. role_target is role.risk-owner because acceptability decisions in this family's variants are scoped to whichever authority is accountable for the specific risk - risk owner is the most representative single role, though variants also exercise other Domain 1 Role & Authority Matrix roles per ROLE + VERB + CONTEXT rather than a fixed hierarchy. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Risk Treatment / Response Selection (Avoid, Mitigate, Transfer/Share, Accept)
teaching_objective: Select the risk treatment (avoid, mitigate, transfer/share, or accept) that best fits the business objective, risk level, cost, and feasibility described in the scenario, rather than defaulting to the strongest control, the cheapest option, or assuming transfer removes accountability.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always selects the treatment that fits the specific business context described (what the scenario actually needs, not a general preference for one treatment type); the tempting wrong answer defaults to the strongest/most comprehensive control, the cheapest option, treats transfer as eliminating accountability, or treats acceptance as passive/unauthorized inaction.
note: PHASE 9B-3 CANDIDATE (D2-U6) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-3 scope. role_target is null because the tempting-wrong pattern is a treatment-selection bias (strongest-control, cheapest-option, transfer-eliminates-accountability, unauthorized-acceptance), not a recurring distractor role. stage_target is stage.risk.treat since all three variants concern treatment selection specifically, deliberately stopping short of residual-risk/validate-acceptability (D2-U7). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Risk Owner vs. Control Owner
teaching_objective: Determine accountability for a specific risk-related decision or action (Risk Owner vs. Control Owner) using ROLE + VERB + CONTEXT, not job title or technical proximity.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always traces the stem's specific verb to the correct accountability - decisions about the risk itself (accepting, selecting a response) belong to the Risk Owner; ensuring/reporting on a control's own operation belongs to the Control Owner; the tempting wrong answer substitutes technical proximity, seniority, or title for that accountability chain.
note: PHASE 9B-4 CANDIDATE (D2-U8) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-4 scope. role_target is null (not fixed to either role) because the family's own invariant reasoning is precisely that the correct role varies by verb/context - a fixed role_target would misrepresent the family's own teaching point. lifecycle/stage are null because ownership accountability is cross-cutting, not tied to one risk-lifecycle stage. One variant illustrates the distinction via an AI-enabled-system scenario, per the approved Phase 9A AI/emerging-risk treatment (scenario variety only, never a dedicated AI-governance topic). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Distinguish inherent risk from residual risk, determine residual risk before judging its acceptability, and route the acceptability decision to the accountable risk/business authority rather than whoever selected or implemented the treatment.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always treats determining residual risk and validating its acceptability as two distinct, ordered steps - never assumes a successfully applied treatment reduces risk to zero, never re-selects treatment or reverses to an earlier stage once residual risk is known, and never defaults risk-acceptance authority to whoever implemented the control; the tempting wrong answer collapses these distinctions.
note: PHASE 9B-4 CANDIDATE (D2-U7) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and Phase 9B-4 scope. stage_target is null at the family level because the three variants deliberately span the Determine-Residual-Risk and Validate-Acceptability stages (and, for the inherent/residual-confusion trap, a reference back to pre-treatment framing), not one single fixed stage, mirroring the same design already used for family.d2.risk-assessment-lifecycle (D2-U2). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Distinguish monitoring (detecting whether the assumptions behind a prior risk decision still hold) from reassessment (updating that decision once something material has changed), recognize genuine reassessment triggers versus routine working-as-designed monitoring, and select report content by what a specific audience needs to decide rather than by activity volume or technical completeness.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always treats a prior risk acceptance as resting on assumptions that must keep being checked, reassesses only when something material has actually changed (not on routine monitoring output or the mere passage of time), and reports the information a specific audience needs to make a decision rather than the most technically complete or highest-volume information available; the tempting wrong answer either treats acceptance as permanently settled, treats normal monitoring activity as itself a reassessment trigger, or reports activity/technical detail instead of a decision-relevant risk statement.
note: PHASE 9B-5 CANDIDATE (D2-U9) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture. stage_target is stage.risk.monitor-reassess for all three variants, since - unlike family.d2.residual-risk-acceptability's deliberate two-stage span - monitoring, reassessment-trigger recognition, and audience-appropriate reporting are all facets of this single closing lifecycle stage, not separate stages of their own. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 2 — Risk Management Synthesis (Embedding Into the Business)
teaching_objective: Apply two or more previously taught Domain 2 reasoning targets together inside one live business-process scenario (a procurement/initiative decision, a business-vs-risk disagreement, a board briefing), recognizing risk management as embedded in normal business decision-making rather than a separate, parallel process.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always brings the applicable risk-management reasoning into the business decision itself - at the earliest point that decision is actually being made - routes genuine business-vs-risk disagreements to the accountable executive authority rather than either party's unilateral view, and selects the smallest, most decision-relevant action that fits what is actually being asked; the tempting wrong answer treats risk management as something that happens before or after the business decision rather than inside it, lets one party's view prevail without escalation, or substitutes a maximal-sounding action (full quantitative recalculation, immediate board escalation, a complete technical inventory) for the action the specific decision actually requires. stage_target is deliberately null: like family.d2.risk-fundamentals (D2-U1) and family.d2.risk-control-ownership (D2-U8), this family is cross-cutting rather than bound to one lifecycle stage - each variant deliberately draws on more than one prior Domain 2 reasoning target at once.
note: PHASE 9B-5 CANDIDATE (D2-U10) — authored by Claude Code per approved Phase 9A Domain 2 architecture and the Phase 9B-4 founder-approved Domain Synthesis / Capstone principle. Exactly one of the three variants (question.d2.0029, the family's anchor/retrieval question) continues the recurring payment-system reference scenario; the other two (question.d2.0030 - a cloud-ERP procurement decision; question.d2.0031 - a regional-expansion board briefing) deliberately use different business settings, per the binding reference-for-comprehension-plus-varied-scenarios-for-transfer rule (docs/learning/CURRICULUM-BLUEPRINT.md) - this family must not become a second payment-system family. Each variant's `concepts` array lists concept.d2.risk-management-embedding-synthesis plus every other Domain 2 concept it genuinely integrates (not just its own), reflecting that these are integrated-practice questions combining multiple previously taught reasoning targets rather than single-concept questions; taught-before-tested is satisfied because D2-U10's prerequisites (D2-U9, D2-U8) transitively cover every one of those referenced concepts (see lesson.d2.risk-management-embedding-synthesis's note for the full prerequisite-closure argument). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that an information security program is the coordinated management structure that turns approved strategy and business objectives into organized execution — not the strategy itself, and not any single technology, tool, or project — and that program resources and priorities must trace back to approved business/security objectives.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always ties the program or resource decision back to what the approved business/security strategy or objectives actually require, coordinating people/process/technology/resources together; the tempting wrong answer treats a single technology deployment, a passive deferral, or an informal/uncoordinated continuation of existing practice as if it were equivalent to having an aligned, coordinated program.
note: DOMAIN 3 CURRICULUM ARCHITECTURE APPROVED / D3-U1 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U1/U2 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong pattern is a technology-first/passive-deferral/informal-continuation shape, not a recurring distractor role. Meridian Manufacturing (the approved recurring reference story) anchors the first variant; the other two variants transfer the same reasoning to a financial-services and a logistics-company setting, per the explicit instruction not to make Meridian the answer to every question. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that classification must reflect business criticality and sensitivity (not cost, threat exposure, or convenience), that an incomplete asset inventory undermines the program's ability to prioritize at all, and that the business owner of an asset — not whoever technically maintains it — is accountable for setting its classification.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always reasons from the asset's business criticality/sensitivity and from accountability resting with the business owner; the tempting wrong answer substitutes a superficial trait (cost, age, technical complexity, or a single threat) for business impact, or substitutes technical proximity/operational familiarity for the accountable owner's decision.
note: DOMAIN 3 CURRICULUM ARCHITECTURE APPROVED / D3-U2 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U1/U2 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis/wrong-role distractor shape varies by variant (technical proximity mistaken for authority; cost mistaken for classification basis; a tool/methodology mistaken for the actual bottleneck), not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant; the other two transfer the same reasoning to a hospital network and a financial-services firm. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that policies, standards, and procedures are binding while guidelines are discretionary, and reason from an artifact's actual governance effect - what it commits the organization to - rather than its title, tone, or formality.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always identifies an artifact's binding or discretionary nature from its own mandatory ('must'/'required') or recommendatory ('should'/'may consider') language and effect; the tempting wrong answer substitutes the artifact's title, formatting, length, issuing authority, or general seriousness of tone for its actual governance effect.
note: DOMAIN 3 U3/U4 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U3/U4 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (title/formatting, issuing-authority, or deferral) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant; the other two transfer the same reasoning to a professional-services firm and a retail chain's vendor program. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Classify and select information security controls by the outcome they are intended to produce in the stated scenario - not by technology, label, or sophistication - and recognize that control design/selection is a risk-driven decision tracing to the actual risk and the enterprise's risk appetite.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always reasons from what the control is actually intended to accomplish in this specific scenario, and from the actual risk/risk appetite driving the decision; the tempting wrong answer substitutes a technology name, label, checklist volume, tool-reported activity, SLA target, or unconditional skip/halt for that reasoning.
note: DOMAIN 3 U3/U4 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U3/U4 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (label/technology, checklist-volume/threat-tooling/SLA, or skip-vs-halt) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant; the other two transfer the same reasoning to a logistics company and a financial-services firm, and the second variant directly recalls Domain 2's risk-driven-prioritization pattern (P08) as reinforcement, not new content. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Distinguish a control that has been implemented from one that is genuinely integrated into the business process it is supposed to protect, and prefer embedding the control into existing operational workflow over a separate, parallel, security-only or compliance-only exercise.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always embeds the control into the existing business workflow itself, at the point where the risk actually occurs; the tempting wrong answer adds oversight, a second parallel process, or documentation alongside the workflow rather than inside it.
note: DOMAIN 3 U5/U6 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U5/U6 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (more oversight without fixing integration, a second parallel process, or documentation mistaken for a working control) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant; the other two transfer the same reasoning to a hospital and a professional-services firm's HR offboarding process - the second of which directly reuses Pattern P09's own approved HR-onboarding/offboarding example scenario. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Distinguish evidence that a control has been implemented or completed as an activity from evidence that it is actually effective at producing its intended outcome, and connect any gap a genuine evaluation reveals back to residual risk the enterprise must decide whether to accept.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always demands evidence of the specific outcome the control was selected to produce; the tempting wrong answer substitutes an activity count, configuration presence, training completion, documentation, cost figure, or compliance-alignment claim for that outcome evidence.
note: DOMAIN 3 U5/U6 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U5/U6 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (activity count, configuration presence, training completion, documentation, cost, or compliance alignment mistaken for outcome evidence) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Distinguish broad security awareness from role-specific training, recognize that delivering either is an activity rather than evidence of changed behavior, and prefer a response that targets the audience's actual risk and evaluates success by behavior change or risk reduction over one that repeats generic content, substitutes documentation/acknowledgment, or reaches for a purely technical fix.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always seeks or produces evidence that behavior tied to the program's specific purpose and audience has actually changed, or takes the concrete step (such as securing leadership support, or reviewing whether requirements still fit current needs) that a genuine program redesign depends on; the tempting wrong answer substitutes a completion/participation fact, a generic one-size-fits-all repeat, an acknowledgment/documentation step, or a purely technical fix for that evidence.
note: DOMAIN 3 U7/U8 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U7/U8 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (premature policy/technical fix, generic-content repetition, or acknowledgment-as-evidence) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant (continuing directly from the Aldergate dual-approval payment control of D3-U5/U6); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a hospital's clinical-workstation behavior and a logistics company's newly promoted warehouse supervisors. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that outsourcing performance of a service does not outsource accountability for its business outcome, that security requirements belong at the start of the vendor relationship, and that a contract or a provider's own claim is not itself the ongoing assurance the enterprise needs - independent verification is.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always keeps accountability with the enterprise and reaches for the enterprise's own verification/oversight of the provider, or the concrete sequencing step that genuinely comes next/first; the tempting wrong answer treats a signed contract, an SLA, a provider claim/certification, or an indemnity clause as if it discharges the enterprise's own responsibility to verify.
note: DOMAIN 3 U7/U8 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U7/U8 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (sequencing error, accountability-transfer assumption, or claim-as-assurance) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant (Aldergate's newly contracted IT-support vendor); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a university's outsourced student-data hosting vendor and a retail chain's outsourced payroll provider - the third of which directly recalls Domain 1's authority-follows-accountability and data-ownership reasoning as reinforcement, not new content. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Select and report program metrics that connect to the program's own objectives and to the specific decision the recipient audience needs to make, distinguishing activity/output measures from effectiveness measures, preferring trend/context over an isolated number, and matching the measurement type (KPI/KRI/KCI/OKR) to the stated reporting need.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always ties the metric back to the program's own objectives and to what the specific recipient needs in order to decide or act, generally preferring a trend over an isolated figure and the measurement type that actually matches the stated need; the tempting wrong answer offers an easy-to-count activity/output figure, an isolated number without trend or objective linkage, the wrong measurement type for the stated need, or the most detailed/technical report regardless of who is actually receiving it.
note: DOMAIN 3 U9/U10 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D3-U9/U10 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (activity-metric substitution, wrong measurement type, or audience mismatch) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Meridian Manufacturing anchors the first variant (the steering committee's first full-cycle report); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a hospital board choosing among KPI/KRI/gap-analysis/incident-statistics, and a regional bank matching an operational vs. strategic report to the correct audience. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Apply two or more previously taught Domain 3 reasoning targets together inside one live business scenario, recognizing the security program as one coordinated management capability rather than nine separate topics, and correctly identifying which management issue (or combination of issues) a real, unlabeled scenario is actually testing.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always integrates every Domain 3 reasoning target the scenario genuinely raises - it does not stop at the first prior unit's answer when the scenario's later facts change what should actually be done; the tempting wrong answer answers from only one prior unit's lens (e.g. only accountability, or only effectiveness) when the scenario requires connecting it to at least one other. stage_target is deliberately null: like family.d2.risk-management-synthesis (D2-U10), this family is cross-cutting rather than bound to one lifecycle stage - each variant deliberately draws on more than one prior Domain 3 reasoning target at once, per docs/learning/LIFECYCLE-MODEL.md's approved, non-canonical Domain 3 conceptual relationship, never a manufactured stage-by-stage lifecycle.
note: DOMAIN 3 U9/U10 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D3-U10, Program Synthesis / Capstone) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-3-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md §10 and the Architect's D3-U9/U10 authoring directive, mirroring the precedent set by family.d2.risk-management-synthesis (D2-U10). Exactly one of the three variants (question.d3.0032, the family's anchor/retrieval question) continues the Meridian Manufacturing reference story, extending its own D3-U5/U6 dual-approval-payment-control narrative into a metrics-and-effectiveness integration; the other two (question.d3.0033 - a hospital outsourced-vendor/asset-classification/accountability scenario; question.d3.0034 - a university awareness/metrics/audience scenario) deliberately use different business settings, per the binding reference-for-comprehension-plus-varied-scenarios-for-transfer rule. Each variant's `concepts` array lists concept.d3.program-synthesis plus every other Domain 3 concept it genuinely integrates, reflecting that these are integrated-practice questions combining multiple previously taught reasoning targets rather than single-concept questions; taught-before-tested is satisfied because D3-U10's prerequisite (D3-U9) transitively covers every D3-U1-U9 concept, since D3-U1 through D3-U9 form one single, unbroken prerequisite chain (see lesson.d3.program-synthesis's own note for the full closure argument). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that incident management readiness - leadership commitment, defined authority, a documented severity/categorization scheme, and tested response capability - must be established before an incident occurs, and that a drafted plan alone does not prove an organization is ready.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always secures or reflects a program-level decision made in advance of any incident - leadership commitment, a categorization scheme, or defined authority - and never lets a drafted-but-untested plan, a technical procedure, or an ad hoc in-the-moment decision substitute for genuine readiness; the tempting wrong answer jumps to technical or staffing detail before the program-level foundation is in place, or treats plan existence itself as sufficient.
note: DOMAIN 4 U1/U2 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U1/U2 authoring directive. This is Domain 4's first production family. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (plan-existence-as-readiness, technical-before-management, or sequencing error) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (launching the hotel chain's first formal incident management program before peak season); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a regional airline (categorization-scheme-first) and a regional insurer (notification-authority decided during plan development). stage_target is stage.incident.prepare because this family's reasoning is genuinely, consistently bound to the Prepare stage across all three variants - unlike the cross-cutting families this domain will also produce (e.g. family.d4.business-impact-analysis-prioritization), which legitimately carry stage_target: null per the Architect's explicit approval. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Determine recovery/response priority from business impact rather than technical sophistication, cost, or novelty; gather that input from the business units that depend on each function; and recognize business impact analysis as the input business continuity planning is built on - and incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery as three distinct plans, not one.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always ties priority to the business impact of disruption, gathered from the people who depend on the function, and correctly distinguishes incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery as answering different questions; the tempting wrong answer substitutes technical sophistication, recency, cost, or an assumption that one plan automatically triggers another. lifecycle and stage_target are deliberately null: a business impact analysis is a cross-cutting input that feeds classification, response, and recovery decisions throughout the incident lifecycle rather than belonging to any single stage, per the Architect's explicit approval not to force this material into a stage merely for symmetry - mirroring the precedent already set by Domain 2's own fully cross-cutting families (e.g. family.d2.risk-fundamentals).
note: DOMAIN 4 U1/U2 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U1/U2 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (technical/novelty/cost substituted for impact, IT-only input, or IR/BCP/DRP confusion) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (a new keyless-entry app assumed to deserve top recovery priority over reservations/payment systems); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a regional water utility (BIA stakeholder input) and a mid-size manufacturer (the IR-vs-BCP boundary, source-confirmed per this batch's required validation - see docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-U1-U2-GATE-RECORD.md). Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that an event must first be confirmed and understood before it is treated as a classified incident, and that severity/category should be assigned by business impact - financial, legal/regulatory, operational, reputational - against a predefined, business-context-tailored scheme, not by technical drama, assumption, or whichever stakeholder reacts loudest.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always confirms what is actually known before acting, and classifies/ranks severity by business impact against a predefined scheme; the tempting wrong answer either acts on an unconfirmed assumption, treats technical sophistication/complexity as if it were business severity, or abandons a consistent classification scheme in favor of generic industry categories, IR-team-alone judgment, or third-party-outsourced judgment. Genuinely bound to stage.incident.identify-confirm of the existing CANONICAL lifecycle.incident - the source material's own Detection and Analysis phase is where a category is assigned, and all three variants stay on that same identify/confirm/classify reasoning rather than drifting into containment or later stages.
note: DOMAIN 4 U3/U4 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D4-U3, Incident Classification / Severity) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U3/U4 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (premature action on an unconfirmed assumption, technical-drama-as-severity, or scheme-abandonment) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (an overnight spike in failed staff-account logins on the reservations system, with the GM assuming chain-wide shutdown and front-desk assuming a routine glitch, before the ISM confirms what is actually known); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a regional grocery chain (technical sophistication vs. actual business impact/data exposure) and a regional courier company (what makes a classification scheme effective). Reuses the existing CANONICAL Pattern P04 (No Lifecycle Jumping, already approved for Domain 4) and P01 (Business Alignment) - no new pattern invented. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that escalation and communication must route decision-relevant, audience-appropriate information through an authorized path - business impact and corrective action to senior management rather than raw technical detail, one pre-authorized spokesperson to media rather than an unplanned comment, and management (not the ISM, the response team, or a third party acting alone) deciding whether/how to notify external parties.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always matches the information to what the specific audience needs to make its own decision, routes external/legal communication through management's authority rather than a technical role acting unilaterally, and never lets an involved third party's own accountability substitute for the organization's own; the tempting wrong answer reports raw technical detail to executives, lets an unauthorized person speak for the organization, or assumes a technical/IR/third-party role can make an external-notification decision that belongs to management. lifecycle and stage_target are deliberately null: escalation and communication recur throughout the incident lifecycle rather than belonging to one stage, per the Architect's explicit approval not to force this family into a single stage merely because it follows classification in sequence.
note: DOMAIN 4 U3/U4 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D4-U4, Escalation & Communications) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U3/U4 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (raw-technical-detail-to-executives, unauthorized-spokesperson, or authority-error on external notification) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (continuing directly from U3's classified incident: what corporate leadership should be told); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a mid-size pharmacy chain (an unauthorized contractor approached directly by a reporter) and a regional telecommunications provider (who decides on regulator/customer notification). Reuses the existing CANONICAL Pattern P11 (Audience-Appropriate Communication) and P02 (Authority Follows Accountability), both already approved for Domain 4 - P11's applicable_domains was extended to include domain.d4 in schema/registry/patterns.json as a narrow, documented metadata change (the pattern's own meaning/recognition_clues/nuance/memory_rule were not altered); see docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-U3-U4-GATE-RECORD.md. No new pattern invented. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that containment limits further harm and spread while preserving the organization's ability to manage the incident properly - choosing a scope proportionate to actual impact rather than an indiscriminate shutdown, acting promptly rather than delaying for root-cause analysis or eradication, and weighing evidence/investigation needs rather than taking a hasty technical action that destroys the evidence needed to understand what happened.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always takes a contained, proportionate action that limits further harm without exceeding what the incident's actual scope requires, without delaying containment to first complete eradication/root-cause work, and without a hasty technical action (reboot, restore, power off) that would destroy evidence: the tempting wrong answer either shuts down far more than the incident affects, waits for root-cause/eradication before containing, or takes an immediate technical action that erases the evidence the organization will need.
note: DOMAIN 4 U5/U6 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D4-U5, Containment) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U5/U6 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (overbroad shutdown, premature root-cause/eradication delay, or evidence-destroying technical action) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (a general manager requesting chain-wide shutdown when only one property's server is affected, continuing directly from D4-U3/U4's classified/escalated incident); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a regional manufacturing company (ransomware on production-line workstations - contain before restore/notify/full-log-review) and a national logistics company (active data exfiltration - block traffic rather than power off, which destroys volatile evidence). ONE family / 3 variants was used because the source material's containment reasoning is genuinely one coherent invariant (proportionate scope + prompt timing + evidence-awareness), not multiple materially different reasoning families - see docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-U5-U6-GATE-RECORD.md. Reuses the existing CANONICAL Pattern P01 (Business Alignment) and P04 (No Lifecycle Jumping), both already approved for Domain 4. No new pattern invented, no registry edit required. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that a reliable understanding of an incident depends on disciplined evidence handling - a documented, unbroken chain of custody, working from copies rather than originals, and appropriate forensic expertise brought in when needed - and that restoring systems or closing out an incident too quickly, before evidence is preserved, can destroy exactly what legal, regulatory, disciplinary, or management decisions later require; deciding whether to involve law enforcement remains senior management's decision, and an outside forensic specialist's involvement does not transfer the organization's own accountability for how the investigation is handled.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always preserves evidence integrity - protecting the chain of custody, working from a copy rather than the original, or prioritizing evidence preservation over a faster but evidence-destroying shortcut - and correctly places law-enforcement-notification authority with senior management rather than the investigator or response team; the tempting wrong answer either rushes to restore/rebuild/analyze the original before evidence is preserved, confuses chain of custody with an unrelated concept (asset ownership, attribution, storage medium alone), or assigns notification/investigation authority to the wrong party. lifecycle and stage_target are deliberately null: the source material's own evidence/investigation reasoning is not bound to a single incident-lifecycle stage - it begins as soon as containment is underway and continues through eradication/recovery decisions, and much of the source's own chain-of-custody/admissibility material is stage-agnostic process guidance rather than tied to one lifecycle moment.
note: DOMAIN 4 U5/U6 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D4-U6, Evidence Handling / Investigation) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U5/U6 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (evidence-destroying restoration shortcut, chain-of-custody-concept confusion, or notification-authority-error) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (IT pressing to reimage/rebuild the affected server immediately, continuing directly from D4-U5's contained incident); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a regional healthcare provider (the PRIMARY reason to maintain chain of custody) and a national retail chain (evidence preservation outranking restoration speed specifically because criminal charges may follow, and law-enforcement-notification authority belonging to senior management). ONE family / 3 variants was used because the source material's chain-of-custody/evidence-integrity reasoning is genuinely one coherent, heavily-repeated invariant across the 4B2/4B1 source material - not multiple materially different reasoning families - see docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-U5-U6-GATE-RECORD.md for the full source-coverage analysis behind this decision. Reuses the existing CANONICAL Pattern P02 (Authority Follows Accountability) and P04 (No Lifecycle Jumping), both already approved for Domain 4. No new pattern invented, no registry edit required. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

teaching_objective: Recognize that eradication (removing the actual cause) and recovery (restoring and verifying normal business operation) are two distinct, sequential steps after containment - neither interchangeable with the other nor with containment itself - that a compromise involving privileged access requires rebuilding from known-clean original media rather than a possibly-tainted backup, and that meeting a stated recovery time objective does not by itself prove recovery is actually complete.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always matches what the scenario has already established has and has not happened - never retreating to re-do a stage already completed (containment, eradication), never jumping ahead to a later stage or to closure before the current one is genuinely finished, and never treating a recovery metric (like RTO) as a substitute for verified, end-to-end business recovery; the tempting wrong answer either skips eradication in favor of a faster restoration shortcut, treats an already-completed stage as still needing to be repeated, or declares the incident resolved prematurely. lifecycle/stage_target: this family is bound to the existing CANONICAL lifecycle.incident but deliberately does NOT set a single stage_target, because its own invariant reasoning genuinely spans two adjacent CANONICAL stages (eradicate, then recover) as one continuous teaching point, and the schema's single-value stage_target field cannot represent that span without misrepresenting half of what the family teaches - a documented, source-grounded deviation from the architecture document's original single-stage assumption, not a default or an oversight.
note: DOMAIN 4 U7/U8 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D4-U7, Eradication / Recovery) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U7/U8 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (backup-instead-of-clean-rebuild, RTO-mistaken-for-full-recovery, or stage-retreat-vs-stage-jump) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (rebuilding the affected reservation server from clean original media rather than a post-compromise backup, continuing directly from D4-U6's preserved evidence); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a regional airline (an RTO met but the business function not actually restored) and a national manufacturing company (malware confirmed removed, systems not yet reconnected - what happens NEXT, testing against both re-doing an already-complete stage and skipping ahead). ONE family / 3 variants was used because the source material's own Knowledge Statement area combines eradication and recovery as one continuous invariant (verify the cause is gone, then verify the business is actually back), not two materially different reasoning families requiring separate treatment - see docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-U7-U8-GATE-RECORD.md for the full source-coverage analysis and the stage_target deviation this required. Reuses the existing CANONICAL Pattern P04 (No Lifecycle Jumping) and P05 (No Lifecycle Reversal), both already approved for Domain 4 - the first genuine full-strength reuse of P05 in Domain 4's production content (D4-U5 uses P04 only; P05 was considered but found not to be D4-U5's actual governing pattern, see DOMAIN-4-U5-U6-GATE-RECORD.md). No new pattern invented, no registry edit required. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.

display_name: Domain 4 — Incident Response / Business Continuity / Disaster Recovery Boundary
teaching_objective: Recognize that incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery are three coordinated but distinct disciplines that can operate at the same time on the same incident depending on what is actually disrupted, and that recovery objectives (RTO, RPO, SDO) describe different dimensions of a business-defined restoration commitment that must be matched to a described scenario by reasoning from the facts, not by recalling which acronym sounds appropriate.
invariant_reasoning: The correct answer always matches the described fact - a disrupted business process to business continuity, an interrupted technology/system to disaster recovery, the security incident itself to incident response, an amount of tolerable downtime to RTO, an amount of tolerable data loss to RPO, and an alternate-mode service level to SDO - and never assumes activating one plan or meeting one recovery metric substitutes for another; the tempting wrong answer reduces business continuity to an IT-only concern, treats the three plans as strictly sequential or automatically co-activating, or swaps one recovery objective's own defining fact for another's. Deliberately cross-cutting (lifecycle: null, stage_target: null): business continuity invocation is one of the CANONICAL incident lifecycle's own documented 'supporting activities that may intersect any stage' (see LIFECYCLE-MODEL.md), and this family's own three variants span recovery-in-progress, backup-strategy-design, and alternate-site-operation - not one lifecycle moment.
note: DOMAIN 4 U7/U8 AUTHORING BATCH CANDIDATE (D4-U8, IR / BCP / DRP Boundary) — authored by Claude Code per the approved docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-CURRICULUM-ARCHITECTURE.md and the Architect's D4-U7/U8 authoring directive. role_target is null because the tempting wrong-basis distractor shape (IT-only BCP reduction, RTO-vs-RPO-vs-SDO confusion) varies by variant, not one fixed role. Harborview Hotels anchors the first variant (front-desk staff using a manual paper check-in process while the reservation server is being rebuilt, continuing directly from D4-U7's recovery-in-progress incident - which plan governs the manual process); the other two transfer the same reasoning to a mid-size hospital system (RPO as the driver of backup frequency, not RTO) and a national telecommunications provider (a warm-site call center restored to half capacity has met the SDO, not the RTO - modeled closely on the source's own clean, reasoning-from-facts scenario). ONE family / 3 variants was used because 'match the described fact to the correct term from a closely related family of terms' is genuinely one coherent invariant reasoning skill, applied first to plans (IR/BCP/DRP) then to recovery metrics (RTO/RPO/SDO) - not two materially different reasoning families; see docs/learning/DOMAIN-4-U7-U8-GATE-RECORD.md for the full source-coverage analysis and the RTO/RPO/SDO/MTO/AIW terminology disposition. Reuses the existing CANONICAL Pattern P01 (Business Alignment, already approved for Domain 4) - every distinction in this unit traces back to what the business itself actually needs, not a technical or IT-driven basis. No new pattern invented, no registry edit required. Not yet human-reviewed or promoted.
